what_its_for: Sodium sulfacetamide is an antibiotic medicine used on your skin. It helps treat acne (pimples and breakouts), seborrheic dermatitis (red, flaky, oily skin or dandruff), and certain skin infections caused by bacteria. It works by stopping the growth of bacteria on your skin.
how_to_take: This medicine is used on the skin only — do not swallow it. Wash your hands before and after using this medicine. Clean and gently dry the area of skin you are treating. Apply a thin layer of the lotion, cream, wash, or foam to the affected area as directed by your doctor. If using the wash, wet your skin first, apply the product, gently massage for 10 to 20 seconds, then rinse off completely and pat dry. Avoid getting this medicine in your eyes, nose, mouth, or on broken or irritated skin. If you accidentally get it in your eyes, rinse thoroughly with water right away.
dosing: The usual dose is to apply this medicine 1 to 2 times per day, or as instructed by your doctor. Follow your doctor's directions exactly, since the dose may be different depending on which skin problem you are treating and which form of the medicine you are using. Do not use more than prescribed, and do not use it more often than your doctor tells you to.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply extra medicine to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and freezing temperatures. Keep the cap or lid tightly closed when not in use. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine if it has changed color, looks unusual, or has passed the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting this medicine in your eyes, mouth, or nose. Do not apply it to cuts, wounds, or severely irritated skin unless your doctor tells you to. Avoid using other skin products, scrubs, or harsh soaps on the treated area without asking your doctor first, as they may cause extra irritation. Try to limit sun exposure on treated skin areas and use sunscreen, since this medicine may make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Do not use this medicine if you are allergic to sulfa drugs (sulfonamides) — check with your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice any of the following: a severe skin rash, hives, blistering, or peeling skin; severe redness, burning, or swelling of the treated area; signs of an allergic reaction such as trouble breathing, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat; your skin condition is getting worse instead of better after a few weeks of use; you accidentally swallow any of this medicine; or you develop a fever, joint pain, or feel generally unwell while using this product.
when_it_works: Many people begin to see improvement in their skin within 2 to 4 weeks of regular use. However, it may take up to 8 to 12 weeks to see the full benefit for acne. Keep using the medicine as directed even if you do not see results right away. If you see no improvement after several weeks, talk to your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before using this medicine, as it should only be used if clearly needed. This medicine is generally not recommended for children under 12 years old unless specifically directed by a doctor. People with kidney disease or a known allergy to sulfa medicines should tell their doctor before using sodium sulfacetamide. Older adults may have more sensitive skin and should use this medicine carefully and report any unusual irritation to their doctor.
